 MSCI +0.95% 
 BTC-USD -5.74%

 Learn more Strategy (MSTR) is back in focus after a special call on November 12, set against fresh disclosures on its Bitcoin buying, preferred share buybacks, and upcoming removal from key MSCI indexes. 
 The recent 1-day share price return of Strategy shows a decline of 6.4%, capping a 7-day fall of 26.2% and a 30-day slide of 33.6%, which lines up with headlines around fresh Bitcoin purchases, MSCI index removal, and preferred share buybacks. Despite this pressure and a year-to-date share price return down 42.5%, longer horizons still show a 3-year total shareholder return of 77.8% and a 5-year total shareholder return of 28.9%, so current momentum is clearly fading rather than building. 
 Scan beyond Strategy and stress test your crypto exposure against a curated 22 cryptocurrency and blockchain stocks that combines listed asset plays with balance-sheet strength and liquidity. 
 Strategy now trades at a deep gap to the average analyst estimate, with the stock near US$90 and targets clustered around US$233. Is that discount signalling mispricing, or a reset that still has room to run? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 34% Undervalued 
 With Strategy last closing at about $90 and the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St putting fair value at $136 based on a discount rate of 8.9%, the current gap reflects a view that market pricing is lagging balance sheet and Bitcoin centric credit ambitions. 
 Management sets an extremely ambitious goal for Strategy to become the world's most valuable company measured by market cap through owning the "most capital" in Bitcoin and issuing the "strongest credit" via Stretch. This long term aspiration depends on continued institutional and banking adoption of Bitcoin, regulatory comfort with tokenised and digital credit structures and the stability of complex capital markets relationships. Any sustained slowdown in bank adoption, regulatory pushback on Bitcoin based credit or loss of confidence after sharp price dislocations such as Stretch's move toward US$70 in June could limit scale, reduce issuance volumes and keep earnings and equity valuation below these aspirations.

 Still, this bearish Strategy narrative could unravel if Bitcoin liquidity weakens for an extended stretch, or if Stretch funding costs climb and squeeze already thin margins.
